'''Alfred Gray''' (October 22, 1939 – October 27, 1998) was an American [[mathematician]] whose main research interests were in [[differential geometry]]. He also made contributions in the fields of [[complex variable]]s and [[differential equations]].

==Short biography==
Alfred Gray was born in [[Dallas, Texas|Dallas]] to Alfred James Gray and Eloise Evans and studied mathematics at the [[University of Kansas]]. He received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1964. His thesis, entitled ''Minimal Varieties and Kahler Submanifolds'', was written under the supervision of [[Leo Sario]] and [[Barrett O'Neill]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alfred Gray|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=13244|website=[[The Mathematics Genealogy Project]]|access-date=2025-11-30}}</ref>

He worked for four years at [[University of California, Berkeley]]. From 1970 until his death he was a professor at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].

He died in [[Bilbao]] of a [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]] while working with students in a computer lab at Colegio Mayor Miguel de Unamuno around 4{{nbsp}}a.m., on October 27, 1998.<ref>{{Cite news|title=OBITUARIES|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1998/11/07/obituaries/5a92f21c-75c0-405b-8188-2eefe498200d/|work=[[The Washington Post]]|date=1998-11-07|access-date=2025-11-30|issn=0190-8286|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Alfred Gray (1939-1998)|url=https://math.umd.edu/old/department/newsletter/newsletter-1998_fall/gray.html|website=[[University of Maryland, College Park]]|access-date=2025-11-30}}</ref>

In 2022 the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] has established the ''Mary and Alfie Gray Award for Social Justice'', named after Alfred Gray and his wife [[Mary W. Gray]], in order to support mathematicians working for human rights.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mary and Alfie Gray Award for Social Justice Established|url=https://www.american.edu/cas/news/mary-and-alfie-gray-award-for-social-justice-established.cfm|website=[[American University]]|date=2022-02-23|access-date=2025-11-30|language=en|first=Patty|last=Housman}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Gray Award|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/gray-award/|website=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|access-date=2025-11-30|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Mathematical contributions==
Gray made several contributions in the classification of various types of [[G-structure|geometric structure]]s, such as [[Kähler manifold]]s and [[almost Hermitian manifold]]s. For instance, together with [[Marisa Fernández|Fernández]] and Gotay, he provided the first example of a symplectic manifold which does not admit a compatible complex structure, hence cannot be Kähler.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Compact Parallelizable Four Dimensional Symplectic and Complex Manifolds|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2047114?origin=crossref|journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|date=1988|pages=1209|volume=103|issue=4|doi=10.2307/2047114|first=Marisa|last=Fernández|first2=Mark J.|last2=Gotay|first3=Alfred|last3=Gray|author-link=Marisa Fernández|author-link3=Alfred Gray (mathematician)|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Among other results, Gray introduced the concept of a [[nearly Kähler manifold]], gave topological obstructions to the existence of geometrical structures, and made several contributions in the computation of the volume of [[Tubular neighborhood|tubes]] and [[Ball (mathematics)|balls]], curvature identities, etc.

He published a book on tubes<ref>{{cite journal|author=Moore, John Douglas|title=Review: ''Tubes'', by Alfred Gray. Addison-Wesley, 1990|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=1992|volume=27|issue=2|pages=311–313|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1992-27-02/S0273-0979-1992-00312-9/S0273-0979-1992-00312-9.pdf|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1992-00312-9|doi-access=free}}</ref> and is the author of two textbooks and over one hundred scientific articles. His books were translated into [[Spanish language|Spanish]], [[Italian language|Italian]], [[Russian language|Russian]] and [[German language|German]].

Gray was a pioneer in the use of [[computer graphics]] in teaching differential geometry (particularly the geometry of curves and surfaces) and of using electronic computation in teaching both differential geometry and [[ordinary differential equation]]s.<ref name=":0" />
